name: Potassium chloride
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Potassium chloride treats or prevents hypokalemia. The kidneys excrete potassium, so kidney impairment sharply raises the risk of hyperkalemia. The US label (oral extended-release tablets) starts patients with kidney impairment at the low end of the dose range and asks for frequent potassium checks; it is contraindicated with triamterene or amiloride. IV concentrate (2 mEq/mL) must be diluted before use; never give by IV push or undiluted (fatal arrhythmia and cardiac arrest reported). In kidney impairment potassium is retained: use the low end of the infusion rate in the IV product label, with ECG monitoring as needed, and recheck potassium after each replacement. Concentration and rate limits: see the IV product label.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses 'renal impairment' without a number; dose is titrated to serum potassium.
chip: CKD: start low; frequent K checks

bands.recommendation: Hypokalemia treatment: 40 to 100 mEq/day in divided doses, no more than 40 mEq per dose; prevention: about 20 mEq/day. Use IV potassium if serum potassium is below 2.5 mEq/L (label).
bands.short: Titrate to K; ≤40 mEq per dose

bands.recommendation: Reduced potassium excretion and a much higher risk of hyperkalemia: start at the low end of the dose range, especially with RAAS inhibitors or NSAIDs; monitor serum potassium frequently and kidney function periodically (label 8.7). IV concentrate: must be diluted; never IV push (see IV label).

hd.text: No dialysis dose in label; potassium removal depends on the dialysate. Give only for documented hypokalemia, start low and check potassium frequently (label 8.7); specialist input. IV concentrate (2 mEq/mL) must be diluted before use; never give by IV push or undiluted (fatal arrhythmia and cardiac arrest reported). In kidney impairment potassium is retained: use the low end of the infusion rate in the IV product label, with ECG monitoring as needed, and recheck potassium after each replacement. Concentration and rate limits: see the IV product label.
hd.short: Only if low K; start low; specialist

pd.text: No PD dose in label. PD patients can become hypokalemic; replace by measured potassium, starting low (label 8.7); specialist input. Hypokalemia is a modifiable risk factor for PD peritonitis (ISPD 2022).
pd.short: Replace by measured K; start low

crrt.text: No data in label; replacement guided by frequent potassium levels and CRRT fluid potassium. Specialist input.

dialyzable: Potassium is removed by hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis (label lists dialysis among hyperkalemia treatments).
monitoring: Serum potassium frequently in kidney impairment and periodically on maintenance; kidney function; magnesium, acid-base status and ECG in cardiac or kidney disease (label 2.1, 8.7).

pediatric.approved_ages: Safety and effectiveness in children not established (oral extended-release tablets; label).

renal.recommendation: Not approved for children; kidney dosing not applicable.
